analysis.title: UBS TECH DAILY CURT COMMENT: Thoughts, DSY into tomorrow, ams, VAT, Technoprobe
key_insights: Curtis says he may have overstayed his bearish view on semis, as he did with software, but sees no catalyst for semis to run and thinks software is too high again.

He wants sell-side analysts to use the Jensen news to cut 2028 semi numbers by about 20%, to close the gap between semi estimates and power/utility estimates. He disagrees that supply-side issues are already discounted after the 'blue sweep' and thinks the bottom comes only when numbers are cut.

Curtis argues that Jensen and most management teams are '100% bullish all the time', so there are no good surprises left. He says an acknowledgement of double and triple ordering could reset expectations. Current sell-side numbers may prove 'correctish', but nearly perfect execution is needed to reach them.

Last week's initial Nvidia debates: how long until negative effects show in products (about 18 months?), more buybacks and less financing of the ecosystem, how much downside is left in the shares, and how bullish this is for AVGO and AMD.

UBS Asia colleagues cite press (UDN) that Nvidia's Vera Rubin ramp has slipped from year-end to 1H27 on HBM4 supply constraints, leaving GB300 as the near-term server mainstay. Hon Hai and Quanta should see limited impact, while 800VDC power, high-end substrate and optical component suppliers could face shipment delays.

VAT: UBS channel checks with industry experts and semi vacuum companies show order momentum remains very strong. UBS expects Q4 26E orders to stay strong and revenue to ramp gradually with a book-to-bill materially above 1x, leaving upside risk to consensus earnings. UBS sees semi WFE capex growth in 2028E.

ams-OSRAM shares fell 10% on results, likely on disappointment over the Q4 revenue guide and few updates on new revenue opportunities. UBS sees upside from balance sheet improvement, with new product revenue as optionality.

ams-OSRAM confirmed it intends to supply the complete optical solution from emitter to packaging. With InP laser optics suppliers booked out to 2029, UBS expects faster adoption of alternatives. UBS sees a possible >€1bn opportunity by 2030, with revenues as early as 2027.

Technoprobe's Q4 guide absorbs a €50m hit from a new ERP system problem, about 2 weeks of sales in the quarter, which explains the gap to consensus. The revenue slips into Q1'27. UBS does not see this as unreasonable given the revenue base is about 4x that of two years ago.

Technoprobe expects most new custom ASIC platforms to ramp next year, requiring vertical MEMS probes. One HBM customer is qualified and two are in progress. About €30m of 2027 revenue is expected from that customer, rising more in 2028 with HBM5e and other customers.
Technoprobe announced a further €150-200m capacity expansion for Q2-Q4'27, which should support €2bn of revenue. UBS's 2027 estimate assumes 85% utilisation, which it calls very conservative.

Dassault Systèmes (DSY) capital markets day (CMD) is tomorrow. Briesty expects the 2029 targets to be maintained. Curtis's view: if DSY keeps its guide, the market will assume it must acquire about €1bn of additional revenue, costing upwards of €5bn. If the market assumes 25%+ value destruction on that, he thinks the stock falls low-to-mid single digits.

The DSY 2024-29 ambition is 7-8% base revenue CAGR, with up to €1bn of incremental cumulative revenue from the UNIV+RSES AI suite. After 2025 results and 4-5% growth guidance for 2026, UBS estimates the ambition implies a 9-13% CAGR over the next three years. ArisGlobal contributes about 80-90bp and UNIV+RSES about 200bp, leaving underlying growth of about 8-10%.

Medidata stabilising revenue trends in Q3 would add about 60-80bp to DSY growth in 2027 relative to 2026. UBS still sees the 8-10% organic ambition as challenging, but expects management may leave it unchanged. Consensus expects a 7% sales CAGR to €8.0bn through 2029 and EPS of €1.72, 9% below the base of the ambition.
DSY's margin ambition is +40-60bp a year over 2024-29. 2025 margin was flat on 2024, and the raised 2026 guidance of +60-80bp leaves DSY needing 50-70bp a year on average for the next three years.
